prompts:
Use case: identity-preserve sprite animation. The attached image is a numbered identity reference board containing SIX already-approved game creatures (read the items left-to-right, top-to-bottom as 1 through 6). Produce ONE TRANSPARENT ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET, exactly FOUR columns and SIX rows (24 isolated full-body sprites). Row N contains only creature N from the reference, repeated in 4 genuinely different locomotion key poses, read left-to-right. Portrait canvas, regular equal-size cells, all sprites fully within their cells with generous transparent gaps. No labels, text, frames, grid lines, scenery or shadows.
Preserve the approved character designs VERY closely: same head and face, materials, palette, slenderness, clothing/weapons, perspective, and simple chunky pixel-art shading. All creatures face to the RIGHT throughout. This is locomotion, not a turntable and not an attack animation. Keep each character's body size and head size absolutely identical across its four cells, keep its torso centered, and keep a consistent invisible ground baseline. Pose changes must come from articulated legs/arms/wings/tail, never from simply stretching, squashing, or translating the whole cutout. Use clear contact, passing/push, opposite contact, and return phases that loop. Feet visibly alternate support vs lift. Ground bodies have modest weight transfer, not a big jump (except the toad). Make pose differences obvious enough to survive reduction to 32px sprites. Transparent alpha background. No extra creatures, no omitted or duplicated rows. Exactly 6 rows x 4 columns.
ROW 1: the slim green bamboo viper; keep its newly approved THIN body. Head stable, lower coil visibly opens/lengthens into a shallow S then pulls back, traveling lateral wave and sweeping red tail, not head bobbing on a static coil.
ROW 2: the squat brown poison toad: four phases of a SHORT HOP, crouch with folded rear thighs / push off with rear legs extending backward / airborne with rear legs trailing / forefeet landing and hindlegs folding. Same broad mouth and raised golden eyes. No inflated throat during locomotion.
ROW 3: the masked leafy vine creature: root-feet alternately lift and reach forward, hooked vine arms counter-swing; keep white mask stable.
ROW 4: the mossy terracotta golem: visibly alternating short-legged steps, one foot planted and other lifted; fists swing opposite to legs. Same squared torso and moss patches.
ROW 5: the tree boss: huge root feet alternately lift and reach, branch arms counter-swing, slight crown sway; same tree face and canopy.
ROW 6: the gray-shouldered terracotta golem: exactly the same stepping mechanics as row 4; retain gray rock shoulder armour.

ROW 1: stone-carrying small ape; the raised rock remains in its hand while its free knuckle and rear feet alternate planted/reaching positions; shambling quadrupedal gait, not throwing.
ROW 2: brown pangolin: pointed snout, overlapping plates and long tail; alternating diagonal pairs of feet step, back gently rolls, long tail counter-swings. Do not turn it into an armadillo or hedgehog.
ROW 3: giant rock-shouldered ape boss: obvious left/right knuckle walking with alternate forearms reaching and planting, hind legs follow; heavy body weight transfer, same white mane and red face.
ROW 4: dark fire crow: strong WINGBEAT cycle with high raised wings / wings half-way down / wings below torso / recovery half-way up. Keep bird torso and head stable, flame tail trailing.
ROW 5: red fox: clear four-legged trot/run cycle with long front/rear leg reach in contact phases, gathered bent legs in passing phases; sharp muzzle, pointed ears, same large fiery tail with small counter-swing.
ROW 6: round furnace spirit: it has two short rocky SIDE ARMS; let them alternately paddle outward/down/back in a hovering travel cycle, tilt slightly in the travel direction and have top flame tips trail differently. Preserve hollow furnace mouth, glowing core and round shell.

ROW 1: lava-cracked terracotta golem: alternating planted/lifted short-legged steps, fists counter-swing, rigid chest, preserve black lava shoulders and orange cracks.
ROW 2: Bifang bird boss: preserve long neck, teal body, red wing edges and exactly ONE visible leg. Clear four-phase WINGBEAT, raised wings / power stroke / wings down / recovery, single leg trails and then gathers. Stable head, no added legs.
ROW 3: ragged undead soldier: asymmetrical limp with one foot braced and other dragging then lifting; sword arm counter-swings, torn banner trails behind, same helmet and broken armour.
ROW 4: spear infantry: two feet alternate forward contact and lifted passing under the hips; keep long spear in both hands with small natural arm swing; plume trails, same broad-brim Chinese helmet.
ROW 5: crescent-blade spirit: preserve the recognizable open crescent silver blade and hanging skull; rock the blade forward/back about 15 degrees across 4 poses while the chain and skull lag in the opposite direction. Do not spin 360 or change into a circular saw.
ROW 6: armoured terracotta golem: alternating planted/lifted feet, counter-swinging fists, same cracked clay body, small gray armour and protruding arrow.

ROW 1: armoured pangolin: same brown plated pangolin with a FEW gray iron plates on its back, alternating diagonal foot pairs and sweeping long tail; do not turn it metallic overall.
ROW 2: headless Xingtian boss: two feet visibly alternate heavy marches, torso and chest face remain headless; round shield and axe counter-swing slightly with stride, never swing axe as an attack.
ROW 3: water ghost: pale face remains stable, flowing blue water-tail curls left/right in a traveling wave, sleeves and two long dark hair locks lag behind the torso. No legs added.
ROW 4: fish demon: obvious alternating tail-fin left/right sweep, pectoral fins paddle backward then recover, slight body yaw without changing right-facing view, same open round fish mouth and red fins.
ROW 5: slender blue jiao dragon: all FOUR short clawed legs visible across gait, alternating diagonal contact pairs, long torso undulates and tail counter-swings. Preserve horns, whiskers, blue fins and slim lizard-like shape.
ROW 6: nine-headed Xiangliu boss: preserve exactly NINE heads and slim necks, head identities and all nine separate throughout. Lower coils alternately extend and gather as it slithers; staggered phase waves through the necks, not all heads bobbing together. Same layered fan composition, blue scales and cream throats.
